title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Gyro)
about: the smallest option, for PCs with little memory (27.6 GB of VRAM + RAM together); lower quality than the 2-3-bit sizes, and the 2-bit Q2_0 decodes faster

title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Gyro)
about: about IQ3_XXS quality with about 20% less GPU memory (35 GB of VRAM + RAM together); decodes about 16-21% slower than Q2_0 on 12 GB cards

title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4)
about: best quality of the NVFP4 versions (GPTQ, sergqwer's strata-nvfp4 pack); RTX 50 has FP4 tensor cores, other NVIDIA cards run it at 8-bit precision

title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4)
about: NVIDIA's own NVFP4 checkpoint (plain rounding), converted by sergqwer; the same size and speed as NVFP4

title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4)
about: NVIDIA's FP4, trained for FP4 (NVIDIA's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local) - slightly faster on short prompts; a 102 GB download that this PC turns into a Strata pack once (about 20-40 minutes, 110 GB more disk); RTX 50 cards have FP4 tensor cores, other NVIDIA cards run it at 8-bit precision. It reads pictures (the shared Qwen3.8-Flash-Next encoder)

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
about: the smaller official version: 138 GB of model + 111 GB n-gram table + 8 GB drafter (257 GB of disk). Runs on a PC with a 12 GB card and 40-64 GB of RAM at about 5-7 tokens a second; quality about 15.5% above the original model's perplexity (code and agent work 5-9%)

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
about: the better official version: 155 GB of model + 111 GB n-gram table + 8 GB drafter (274 GB of disk, 17 GB more than 2.00). About the same speed; quality about 7.3% above the original model's perplexity (code and agent work 2-3%)

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
about: the smallest official version: 121 GB of model + 111 GB n-gram table + 8 GB drafter (239 GB of disk, 18 GB less than 2.00). Runs where 2.00 is tight (a 12 GB card and 32-40 GB of RAM). Smallest: fine for code and agent work, noticeably weaker on plain prose; pick 2.00 if it fits

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
about: Unsloth Dynamic 8-bit: the experts in MXFP4 as DeepSeek made them, the rest in BF16 (the checkpoint's own precision); 508 GB, for machines with hundreds of GB of RAM or several cards
